body.statement: Uniformly over the instrumental fixed-radius subclass \(P\in\mathcal M\), the construction in \(\texttt{def:cross-fitted-primitive}\) satisfies \(\max_k\|\widehat h_k-h\|_{\infty}=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n})\) for \(h\in\{p,g,m,r\}\), where \(\beta=1/2-(d+1)/(4s)>5/12\), and \(\|\widehat\theta'-\theta'\|_{\infty,J}=O_P(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n})\), where \(\beta_1=1/2-(d+3)/(4s)>0\). These are consequences to be proved from the strengthened fixed-radius conditions, not assumptions imported from a comparator.
body.justification: This derives concrete nuisance rates on the explicitly instrumental smooth subclass before checking them against the separate Gumbel-scale remainder threshold.
body.gap: Doss (2026) formulates pointwise product-remainder conditions and Takatsu and Westling (2025) analyze different local-linear uniform remainders; neither source assumes or supplies this proposal's common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) class.
body.consumer: The displayed exponents can guide a future fully specified implementation, but are not yet a theorem about the frozen learner map.

obligation.what_is_open: A theorem for the frozen learner requires a fully specified sample map: a kernel, boundary moment system, density-normalization map, and output on singular empirical Gram matrices.
obligation.obstruction: The symbol for the nuisance learner names a family of boundary-corrected local-polynomial procedures rather than one measurable estimator. Uniform inverse and derivative bounds therefore cannot be asserted for the named object itself.
obligation.attempted: The boundary dimension, bias, stochastic term, derivative cost, both exponents, and stability of quotient and integration operations were derived for every regular complete implementation satisfying explicit moment-matrix conditions.
obligation.partial_result:
Put \(D=d+1\).  For a completely specified boundary local-polynomial estimator whose kernel is bounded and compactly supported, whose polynomial degree is at least \(\lceil s\rceil\), whose population boundary moment matrices have a common positive eigenvalue lower bound, and whose empirical singular-matrix convention is declared, Taylor expansion and a uniform Bernstein bound give, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \left\|\partial_a^j\widehat h_k-\partial_a^j h\right\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(h_n^{s-j}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D+2j}}}\right).
\]
At \(h_n=n^{-1/(2s)}\), the stochastic term is the slower term.  Thus
\[
 \|\widehat h_k-h\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad \beta=\frac12-\frac{d+1}{4s},
\]
and
\[
 \|\partial_a\widehat m_k-\partial_a m\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad \beta_1=\frac12-\frac{d+3}{4s}.
\]
The model restriction \(s>3(d+1)\) implies
\[
 \beta>\frac12-\frac1{12}=\frac5{12},
 \qquad
 \beta_1>\frac12-\frac{d+3}{12(d+1)}>0.
\]
The lower density bounds in \(\texttt{ass:p-bounds}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\) make division locally Lipschitz on the relevant range, and integration over the unit covariate cube is a contraction in the supremum norm.  Hence quotient formation and the displayed marginal integration preserve these orders.  This calculation proves the advertised exponents for every implementation satisfying the stated regularity properties.  It is not yet a theorem about \(\widehat\eta\): the frozen description does not select a kernel, write the boundary moment equations or normalization map, or declare the estimator on a singular empirical Gram matrix, so it does not specify a unique sample map to which the probability assertion can be applied.
